design_summary.purpose: motor_control_top is the synthesizable top-level ASIC wrapper for the doMINO_aeroguard_ctrl control-and-safety path. It owns the compact 64-bit cfg_bus register window, request packaging, response validation, timeout supervision, actuator clamping, deterministic safe fallback, and status aggregation required to interface with an external NVIDIA DoMINO Automotive Aero service using only compact descriptors and control/status transactions.
design_summary.operating_model: The design operates as a single-clock-domain synchronous controller. It accepts configuration through cfg_bus, issues a compact request only when enabled and idle, waits for a compact response, validates sequence and freshness policy, supervises timeout age, clamps the derived actuator command, and switches to a deterministic safe fallback command on timeout, stale/invalid response, protocol/configuration fault, or persistent downstream not-ready conditions. It does not compute aerodynamics internally and does not expose raw geometry, mesh, STL, flow-field, or tensor payloads on top-level pins.

external_interfaces.name: cfg_bus
external_interfaces.intent: Compact configuration and status access for software-visible control, policy updates, and readback.

external_interfaces.name: request_response_sideband
external_interfaces.intent: Launch and accept compact request/response descriptors without exposing bulk payloads.

external_interfaces.name: actuator_command_sideband
external_interfaces.intent: Deliver validated and clamped actuator commands or deterministic safe fallback commands.

external_interfaces.name: safety_status
external_interfaces.intent: Expose supervisory health, fallback, rejection, timeout, and configuration-fault status.

module_architecture.name: register_file_64b
module_architecture.role: 64-bit cfg_bus register-file and policy gate for enable, soft reset, mode selection, timeout threshold, freshness threshold, actuator clamp limits, sequence seed/control, status control, and safe-fallback configuration.
responsibilities: Implement the 64-bit cfg_bus window semantics.
Expose semantic configuration outputs for downstream control blocks.
Reject configuration changes that would violate safety constraints.
Provide readback of current config and status.
Emit write-fault indication on invalid writes.
interface_notes: Consumes cfg_bus_addr, cfg_bus_wdata, cfg_bus_wen, and cfg_bus_ren and returns cfg_bus_rdata and cfg_bus_rvalid.

Owns configuration-facing outputs including cfg_enable, cfg_soft_reset, cfg_mode, cfg_timeout_threshold, cfg_freshness_threshold, cfg_act_min, cfg_act_max, cfg_seq_seed, cfg_safe_fallback, cfg_status_clear, and cfg_fault_write.
Accepts status_flags_in and fault_in for readback composition and fault propagation.
Does not drive request, response, actuator, or bulk-data interfaces.
ownership_notes: Committed configuration image and policy-safe write handling belong here.
Small control/status registers are allowed; no raw geometry or tensor storage is represented.
Filename is fixed as register_file_64b.v.

module_architecture.name: request_fsm
module_architecture.role: Synchronous request issue FSM that forms compact request descriptors when enabled and idle.
responsibilities: Issue compact request descriptors.
Generate and increment sequence identifiers under control of the outstanding transaction state.
Select compact geometry and flow descriptors rather than raw data.
Assert req_valid only when a new transaction is ready.
Respect downstream req_ready backpressure.
interface_notes: Consumes cfg_enable, cfg_soft_reset, cfg_mode, cfg_seq_seed, cfg_safe_fallback, outstanding_seq, busy_in, and req_ready.
Produces req_data, req_valid, req_seq_out, req_geom_handle, req_flow_id, req_ctrl_flags, and req_launch.
req_data is compact and limited to 64 bits or less.
The block blocks issuance while busy, awaiting response, or under fallback rules unless safe-mode emission is explicitly permitted by policy.
ownership_notes: Request sequencing and launch intent belong here.
Compact handles or indices are used instead of raw mesh expansion.
Filename is fixed as request_fsm.v.

module_architecture.name: response_validator
module_architecture.role: Compact response acceptance and validation block.
responsibilities: Validate response sequence number against the outstanding request.
Check freshness and age against programmable policy.
Reject timeout, malformed, or protocol-violating responses.
Provide compact validated summary information only.
Raise stale and fault indications for supervisory logic.
interface_notes: Consumes resp_data, resp_valid, outstanding_seq, cfg_freshness_threshold, cfg_timeout_threshold, elapsed_age, and timeout_expired.
Produces validated_valid, validated_seq_match, validated_summary, validated_flags, reject_stale, and reject_fault.
Consumes only compact response descriptors and actuator-relevant summary information; it does not assume or emit full flow-field tensors.
ownership_notes: Response acceptance and protocol checking are localized here.
Sequence mismatch maps to stale rejection; protocol or timeout issues map to fault rejection.
Filename is fixed as response_validator.v.

module_architecture.name: timeout_counter
module_architecture.role: Small synchronous age and timeout tracking counter used for staleness guard and response-time policy.
responsibilities: Count request age while a transaction is outstanding.
Reset age on accepted response or new request launch.
Assert timeout and stale indications at threshold crossings.
Provide compact age information to the validator and fallback controller.
interface_notes: Consumes cfg_timeout_threshold, cfg_freshness_threshold, req_launch, and resp_accept.
Produces elapsed_age, timeout_expired, and stale_expired.
Counter-based tracking is intentionally small and synchronous.
ownership_notes: Age tracking is compact and timing-friendly.
No memory-like bulk structures are inferred.
Filename is fixed as timeout_counter.v.

module_architecture.name: clamp_unit
module_architecture.role: Actuator clamp and optional deterministic safe-command shaping block.
responsibilities: Convert validated compact summary into compact actuator command.
Clamp actuator command within configured minimum and maximum bounds.
Flag clamp violations when clamping is necessary.
Provide deterministic safe fallback command output.
interface_notes: Consumes validated_summary, validated_flags, cfg_act_min, cfg_act_max, cfg_safe_fallback, and fallback_active.
Produces cmd_raw, cmd_clamped, clamp_violation, and safe_cmd.
act_cmd_data is derived from summary-to-command mapping and clamp logic, not raw physics fields.
ownership_notes: Clamp enforcement belongs here before any command is marked valid.
Safe command is deterministic after reset and after fault entry.
Filename is fixed as clamp_unit.v.

module_architecture.name: fallback_controller
module_architecture.role: Safe-fallback controller that asserts deterministic safe operation on timeout, stale response, protocol/configuration fault, or persistent downstream not-ready conditions.
responsibilities: Enter fallback on timeout, stale rejection, protocol fault, or write-fault conditions.
Provide deterministic safe-command selection gating.
Assert fault output whenever fallback is active or a fault condition is present.
Allow safe-command issuance according to policy under fallback state.
interface_notes: Consumes timeout_expired, reject_stale, reject_fault, clamp_violation, cfg_fault_write, downstream_ready, and safe_cmd_in.
Produces fallback_active, fault_out, cmd_select_safe, and cmd_force_valid.
This block governs whether safe fallback is selected and whether a safe command may be forced valid under policy.
ownership_notes: Deterministic fallback state is owned here.
fault_out is sourced from fallback supervision.
Filename is fixed as fallback_controller.v.

module_architecture.name: status_aggregator
module_architecture.role: Aggregates configuration, timeout, validation, clamp, fallback, and transaction state into compact status flags and register readback data.
responsibilities: Aggregate current enable, mode, timeout, freshness, clamp, sequence, age, and fault state.
Provide compact status flags for readback.
Format cfg_bus_rdata readback words for the register window.
Keep all outputs compact and implementation-friendly.
interface_notes: Consumes configuration and supervisory state including cfg_enable, cfg_soft_reset, cfg_mode, cfg_timeout_threshold, cfg_freshness_threshold, cfg_act_min, cfg_act_max, outstanding_seq, elapsed_age, timeout_expired, stale_expired, validated_valid, reject_stale, reject_fault, fallback_active, and fault_out.
Produces status_flags_out and cfg_bus_rdata.
Provides software-visible summary without exposing geometry, flow fields, or model tensors.
ownership_notes: This block summarizes state only; it does not generate control decisions.
It supports register readback consistency for the committed configuration image.
Filename is fixed as status_aggregator.v.

interface_summary.intent: Provide the configuration window access path and feed back summarized status and fault context for committed register readback and policy gating.
Export committed configuration and readback outputs for downstream supervision, request formation, validation thresholds, and safety behavior.
Deliver control-policy inputs and outstanding-transaction context used to decide whether a new compact request may be launched.
Provide compact request descriptor fields and launch indication for the external service interface and downstream timeout supervision.
Provide the outstanding sequence, policy thresholds, and age/timeout context required to validate compact responses.
Return compact validation results, summary data, and rejection indications for command generation and fallback supervision.
Drive age tracking from request launch and accepted response events under the configured supervisory thresholds.
Provide compact age, timeout, and staleness status used by validation, fallback, and status aggregation.
Supply validated summary data, actuator clamp policy, and fallback state for command derivation and safe-command shaping.
Return compact raw and clamped actuator commands plus clamp-violation and safe-command outputs.
Provide all fault and readiness conditions that can force or sustain deterministic safe fallback operation.
Expose fallback state, safe-command selection, and top-level fault indication for actuator control and status aggregation.
Provide the committed configuration and supervisory state used to generate compact software-visible status and readback formatting.
Return compact status flag summaries and cfg_bus readback words for software inspection and integration visibility.

data_flow_summary: Software programs the compact cfg_bus window with enable, soft reset, mode, timeout threshold, freshness threshold, actuator clamp bounds, sequence seed, safe-fallback command, and status-control fields.

When enabled and idle, request_fsm forms a compact request descriptor with sequence, compact geometry handle or descriptor reference, compact flow-condition identifier or descriptor reference, and control flags.
timeout_counter starts or refreshes age tracking on request launch and response acceptance, producing elapsed age and timeout/stale indications.
response_validator accepts only compact response descriptors, checks sequence match and freshness policy, and rejects stale, malformed, protocol-violating, or timeout-expired responses.
clamp_unit maps validated compact summaries into a compact actuator command, then clamps the result to configured min/max bounds and supplies a deterministic safe command for fallback.

fallback_controller asserts fallback_active and fault_out on timeout, stale rejection, protocol/configuration fault, clamp violation, or persistent downstream not-ready conditions, and selects safe-command issuance under policy.
status_aggregator composes the committed configuration image, age, validation results, fallback state, and fault state into status_out and cfg_bus readback data.
The top-level interface remains compact and does not carry raw geometry, mesh, STL, flow-field, pressure-map, or surrogate-tensor payloads.

clock_reset_summary.clocking: The RTL assumes a single synchronous clock domain on clk. All request, response, timeout, clamp, fallback, register, and status functions are synchronous to clk. If asynchronous integration inputs are introduced later, they must be synchronized before use at the integration boundary.
clock_reset_summary.reset_behavior: On reset_n deassertion, all outstanding transaction state is cleared, request and command valids are cleared, the controller enters deterministic safe fallback, and conservative safe actuator defaults are loaded. The design shall not emit a non-safe actuator command until a valid response has been accepted and validated.

integration_notes: The intended external service link is compact request/response transport to an external NVIDIA-hosted worker; no internal aerodynamics computation is performed in RTL.
The automotive_aerodynamics context may reference stream velocity 38.89 m/s, STL geometry format, and DrivAerML reference geometry only as configuration context, not as top-level payloads.
Total scalar-equivalent top-level I/O is kept compact by using cfg_bus plus valid/ready sidebands and compact command/status outputs.

Any future on-chip payload storage must use sky130_sram_1kbyte_1rw1r_32x256_8 only, with the required collateral gate before instantiation; no substitution with flip-flop arrays or inferred memories is permitted for bulk payload storage.
Assertions are expected for stale-response rejection, clamp enforcement, and fallback entry on timeout, consistent with the safety wrapper role.
consistency_notes: No hierarchy, ports, or filenames may differ from digital_spec_json.
motor_control_top is the required synthesizable top module and is retained as the design top.
The specification is treated as the single source of truth; no new modules or ports are introduced.
